name: Ling Cage Style Sci-Fi Short
description: Develops an inspiration, character settings, reference assets or a script into a Ling Cage style semi-realistic 3D post-apocalyptic sci-fi animated short, advancing in stages through the story script, storyboard, key elements, shot-by-shot video and audio layers.

planning.planning_notes: Dynamic execution path: first judge the entry point from total_duration, output_language, director_style, asset_mode, audio_mode, the user input and the canvas/uploaded assets, and lock the creative specification at the Skill level: default 16:9, 24fps, 720p, target duration, output language, director style, asset strategy, whether to generate BGM, and visual style; this specification does not create a standalone node. If the user has only keywords or an inspiration, first produce several story directions to choose from, then expand into a scene-by-scene script and make the story-stage output clear and reviewable; if the user already has a complete script, the direction selection may be skipped but a structured extraction must be done. After the story stage is complete, generate the storyboard, outputting Key Elements, the Shot List and the BGM plan, and check whether every shot binds its scene, characters, action, dialogue/narration, duration and transition intent. After the storyboard is complete, enter the key element image stage: first list from the Key Elements the independent assets that need to be reused across shots, then create a separate draft node for each asset. Each recurring character or team is its own node; each main reused scene is its own node; each monster, machine, core prop, or environment source that needs a consistent appearance across shots is its own node. Character nodes generate a three-view sheet, scene nodes generate a 2x2 four-panel grid without characters, and monster/machine/prop nodes generate a complete-structure or multi-angle reference; bind the user's assets first, and when they do not match, remake the style from the original asset. Do not create just one generic "key elements" node, and do not merge multiple independently referenceable characters, scenes, monsters, machines or props into one overview image; only assets that are always referenced downstream as one whole may share a node. After the key elements are complete, create single-shot videos per Shot List entry or explicit scene segment: every Shot List entry must be an independent video intent item and canvas node, each shot 4-15 seconds, each shot referencing only the character, scene and monster/machine/prop element images it actually needs; dialogue and sound effects are written into the corresponding video prompt, and narration and in-shot ambient sound are likewise expressed through the shot prompt, without creating separate audio nodes; image references do not exceed 9 and audio references do not exceed 3, and the previous shot's video is referenced only when strongly continuous. The Runner executes only nodes that have landed on the canvas and will not automatically expand later nodes from a completed script or storyboard, so the complete draft must list the key element nodes and all single-shot video nodes at once, and create a BGM audio node only when a score is needed. If audio_mode is "Generate BGM", create a BGM audio node only when a score is needed; if it is "Do not generate BGM", do not create a standalone audio node. Finally, remind the user that final composition can be done on the canvas and ask whether upscaling is needed; final composition and upscaling are handled by canvas tools.
planning.prompt_guide: Output uses clear Markdown in the same language as the user's input. The core style is Ling Cage-flavored semi-realistic 3D CG cinematic post-apocalyptic sci-fi: realistic-grade rendering, a slightly animated aesthetic, oppressive dark tones, wasteland poetry, grimy worn materials, volumetric light, the Tyndall effect, real skin and battle-damaged gear. Scene directions can revolve around spaces such as the surface wasteland, the interior of the Lighthouse, the Mana ecosystem and Dragon Bone Village, keeping spatial relationships, light colors, activity areas and environment states continuous. Subtitles are forbidden by default at the Shot level; narration and dialogue must not overlap; user assets are bound first, and are generated/remade only when missing or stylistically mismatched.
conduct_rules: Create the complete workflow draft first; the story direction/script, creative specification, storyboard, key element batch, scene-segment videos and the necessary BGM audio node must each have a clear stage output, and the actual pace of continuing, retrying and executing is controlled by the canvas workflow.
Default 16:9, 24fps, 720p; the target duration follows the input total_duration, with a default range of 1-3 minutes.

Characters must be semi-realistic 3D CG, with tactical gear, scratches, dust, blood stains and real materials made explicit; Japanese-anime flat shading, chibi style, bright-and-clean looks and excessive cyber neon are forbidden.
Scenes must distinguish the surface wasteland, the interior of the Lighthouse, the Mana ecosystem and Dragon Bone Village, and annotate light colors, spatial relationships and activity areas.
The storyboard must contain scene, story beat, shot size, camera height, camera movement, character orientation and transition intent.

The key element stage must not create just one generic "key elements" node. Every recurring character or team, every main reused scene, and every monster/machine/core prop/environment source must be its own node; do not replace multiple independent elements with one overview image.
Every Shot List entry must be an independent video intent item and canvas node; creating just one generic "single-shot video" node to stand in for the complete short is not allowed.

Before video generation, check shot by shot: scene reference, character references, dialogue/narration text, in-shot ambient sound, action sound effects, key actions and image references <=9; dialogue, narration and in-shot sound effects should be written into the corresponding video prompt.
Character wounds, equipment damage and environment state must stay continuous across shots and must not reset automatically.
Narration and character dialogue must be staggered and must not repeat each other semantically; dialogue-dense shots usually get no narration; BGM is handled only as a standalone score audio node.
The creative specification serves planning only and creates no standalone node; at the end of the flow, only remind the user to compose on the canvas and ask whether upscaling is needed.

rating_bands.description: The stages are clearly separated, the style lock is stable, asset binding is complete, and shot rhythm, combat staging, emotional performance and audio staggering are all clearly landed in the outputs.
The flow is basically complete, but some stages lack asset analysis, key element binding, shot-by-shot checks, transition intent, audio staggering or style taboos.
Confirmation is skipped, a Japanese-anime / chibi / bright-and-clean style is used, or reference counts, character continuity and audio conflicts are ignored.

visual_review_items.name: Semi-realistic post-apocalyptic style
visual_review_items.description: The picture should be a semi-realistic 3D CG cinematic look, with oppressive dark tones, grimy real wear, volumetric light and wasteland poetry coexisting.

visual_review_items.name: Key element consistency
visual_review_items.description: The character three-views, scene four-panel grids and monster/prop references must become cross-shot appearance anchors.

visual_review_items.name: Clear shot space
visual_review_items.description: Combat and movement directions obey the axis, geographic relationships, character orientation and continuity of the environment state.

text_review_items.name: Stage boundaries
text_review_items.description: Each main stage has a clear output, input dependencies and next step, making it easy to review and advance the canvas workflow.

text_review_items.name: Audio rules
text_review_items.description: The time ranges, responsibilities and conflict avoidance of narration, dialogue, BGM and SFX must be clear.

domain_constraints: Do not use Japanese-anime flat shading, chibi monsters, bright-and-clean looks or magic-effect vocabulary.
Video shots reference at most 9 images and at most 3 audio clips.
Shot level defaults to no subtitles; subtitles are handled only as an optional track in post-production.
